paragraphs.text: Anthropic launched the roadshow for its initial public offering on November 10, 2026, setting an expected price range of $70 to $78 per share, the company said in an announcement. The offering covers 825 million shares of Class A common stock: 801,351,354 sold by Anthropic and 23,648,646 sold by existing stockholders.

Reuters reported that the deal could raise up to $64.4 billion. Based on the outstanding shares listed in the filing, Reuters calculated a valuation of up to $1.02 trillion. The company has applied to list on the Nasdaq Global Select Market under the ticker ANT, with Goldman Sachs and Morgan Stanley leading the offering.
A day after a withdrawn filing

The new range follows an unusual episode on November 9. According to emails seen by Reuters, IPO details were briefly sent to investment banks late that Monday and then retracted. The earlier figures had put the price at up to $80 a share, so the top of the new range is $2 lower.

Anthropic's last private valuation was $965 billion, Reuters said. Some potential investors had pushed for a more attractive price, and a recently discussed figure of $1.5 trillion was seen by some as the high end of expectations. AFP, in a report carried by Malay Mail, said the expected valuation of more than $1 trillion is down from an earlier high of $2 trillion.

Alongside the public offering, AMD, Broadcom, Google, Micron, Microsoft, Nvidia and a TSMC entity agreed to buy $26 billion of stock at the IPO price in a private placement, according to the filing as reported by RTTNews. Reuters said that with all of these cornerstone investments included, the total offering could raise up to $90.4 billion. Anthropic also expects to give underwriters a 30 day option to buy up to 123.75 million additional shares.

The filing shows fast growth and heavy spending. Third quarter revenue rose 47% from the prior quarter to $16.96 billion, Reuters reported, a slowdown from growth of 144% in the quarter before. Commitments for computing power total about $900 billion, including deals with Amazon and Google. A separate Reuters analysis said revenue in the first half of 2026 reached $16.29 billion, about 14 times the level a year earlier.

The listing comes at a difficult moment for technology stocks. Reuters noted that the Nasdaq had its deepest one day drop in 19 months on the Thursday before the roadshow, amid scrutiny of AI spending after Democratic gains in the midterm elections. The prospectus warns that rivals could gain an edge by building models faster and that advances in AI could outpace safety measures.

Anthropic was founded in 2021 by former OpenAI researchers, including chief executive Dario Amodei and his sister Daniela Amodei, and makes the Claude family of models. It is a public benefit corporation, and Reuters reported that a single Class F share controlled by its seven co-founders carries 50.1% of the voting power on key matters.

The range is a compromise. At the top end the valuation sits only slightly above the last private round, which suggests Anthropic chose a price that public investors can accept after weeks of pressure on AI stocks rather than chasing the higher figures discussed earlier in the year. The $26 billion from suppliers and cloud partners gives the deal a large base of committed demand before the order book opens.

The final price, set at the end of the roadshow, will show whether demand pushed Anthropic toward the top of the $70 to $78 range or forced it lower, a signal for every AI company planning to go public.
